gaps.sentence: The train ___ faster than the bus, so we always take the train.
gaps.explanation: Timeless comparisons take the present simple: goes.

gaps.sentence: Look at Sam — he ___ at that stranger again.
gaps.hint: look draws attention to this moment
gaps.explanation: 'Look' draws attention to something happening now, so the present continuous is used: is staring.

gaps.sentence: I usually cycle to work, but this week I ___ the bus because my bike is being repaired.
gaps.hint: this week contrasts with the usual habit
gaps.explanation: 'But this week' signals a temporary arrangement around now, so the present continuous is correct: am taking.

gaps.sentence: It is the first time I ___ paella.
gaps.hint: it is the first time takes present perfect
gaps.explanation: After 'It is the first time', English uses the present perfect: have eaten.

gaps.sentence: I ___ in this city since 2015, and I still love it.
gaps.hint: since 2015 plus still means it continues
gaps.explanation: 'Since 2015' with 'still' marks a situation continuing to the present, so the present perfect is used: have lived.

gaps.sentence: At midnight, the protesters ___ outside the parliament, refusing to move.
gaps.hint: at midnight, in progress at that point
gaps.explanation: An action in progress at a specific past moment takes the past continuous: were standing.

gaps.sentence: When we were students, we ___ to live on instant noodles.
gaps.hint: a past habit with used to
gaps.explanation: 'Used to' plus the infinitive describes a past habit: used to live.

gaps.sentence: At the moment, the council ___ whether to sell the library.
gaps.hint: at the moment shows an ongoing process
gaps.explanation: 'At the moment' marks an ongoing process, so the present continuous fits: is deciding.
